title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the continuation of the Longue Marche, a study of the 'équation des lacets', i.e. the defining relations of what is now Drinfeld's Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT. Notation: π = π_{0,3} is the free group on two generators, the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. 𝔖_{0,3} is the extended (non-oriented) cartographic group: π extended by the order-12 symmetry group S_3 × Z/2 of the 'triangle'. σ_∞ is the involution swapping 0 and 1. ρ is the order-3 rotation, treated on the previous page.

The page continues the analysis of the order-2 equation (35): h·σ_∞(h) = 1. In GT language this is the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1.

1. Reduction to non-abelian H^1. Solutions of (35) are 1-cocycles of Z/2 = ⟨σ_∞⟩ with values in π. The claim (36) is that every solution is a coboundary, h = β·σ_∞(β)^{-1}, with β ∈ π unique. Two facts are used:
- the fixed-point set of σ_∞ on U_{0,3} (the universal covering / 'universal map' on which π acts freely) is a single point, (37);
- consequently the centraliser π^{σ_∞} is {1}.
The standard argument: complements of π in π⋊⟨σ_∞⟩ correspond to fixed points. A unique fixed point gives H^1(Z/2, π) = 1, and π^{σ_∞} = 1 gives uniqueness of β.

2. Profinite version (38). He 'admits' the analogous statements for the profinite completion π̂_{0,3}: (π̂)^{σ_∞} = 1, and (from the previous page) every finite-order element of the completed cartographic group is conjugate to a discrete one. These yield H^1(Z/2, π̂) = 1 with unique β ∈ π̂. He notes this is a stronger assumption than what was admitted for ρ.

3. Allowing β in the whole cartographic group. Formulas (39)/(40) compute the centraliser of σ_∞ in Γ_{0,3} (equivalently in 𝔖_{0,3}): it is the Klein group Z/2 × Z/2 = {1, σ_∞, τ_∞, τ'_∞ = σ_∞τ_∞}. Here τ_∞ is the orientation-reversing reflection.
- If β is allowed in 𝔖_{0,3}, then h = β·σ_∞(β)^{-1} = βσ_∞β^{-1}σ_∞^{-1} determines β only up to right multiplication by this centraliser.
- Hence (41): β = β_0 σ_∞^ε τ_∞^{ε'}, with ε, ε' ∈ Z/2 and β_0 the solution in π.

4. Next page: β lies in the orientation-preserving part (written GT^+_{0,3}) iff ε' = 0.

Purpose: parametrise solutions of the 2-cycle relation for f ∈ GT by 'square roots' β. This is the analogue of the modern statement that f satisfying f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 can be written f = g(y,x)^{-1}g(x,y).
errors: In (39) the generators are written 'σ_∞, τ' and later corrected to σ_∞, τ_∞; τ'_∞ should be σ_∞τ_∞. These are notational slips, not mathematical ones.

The profinite statements are explicitly 'admitted' rather than proved: triviality of (π̂_{0,3})^{σ_∞}, and conjugacy of finite-order elements of the completed group to discrete ones. They are true; they follow from results on torsion and centralisers in profinite free products (Herfort–Ribes type) or from profinite Bass–Serre arguments. They are, however, gaps on this page.
The phrase 'd'ordre (2)_1' is garbled; the indeterminacy group has order 4 (Klein group).

ideas.what: Solutions of the order-2 loop equation h·σ(h) = 1 in the free group are exactly coboundaries h = β σ(β)^{-1}, with β unique, deduced from uniqueness of the fixed point of σ on the universal cover and trivial centraliser.
ideas.modern_name: Vanishing of non-abelian H^1(Z/2, F_2) for an involution with a unique fixed point; parametrisation of the 2-cycle relation f = g(y,x)^{-1}g(x,y)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for the pro-unipotent case; Lochak–Schneps / Ihara for the profinite GT case
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished 'Longue Marche' sequel notes; not in the Esquisse

ideas.what: Extending the result to the profinite completion requires that finite-order elements of the completed cartographic group are conjugate to discrete ones and that centralisers are trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Torsion and centralisers in profinite free products (profinite Bass–Serre theory)

ideas.what: The centraliser of σ_∞ in the extended cartographic group 𝔖_{0,3} is a Klein 4-group, giving a 4-fold indeterminacy of β; orientation is detected by the τ_∞-exponent.
ideas.modern_name: Centraliser of a transposition in S_3 × Z/2 acting on the profinite free group; the GT vs \hat{GT}^{±} (extended GT) distinction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; extended GT studied by Lochak–Schneps and others

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently derives the 'square-root' parametrisation of solutions of the 2-cycle relation via a fixed-point / non-abelian-cohomology argument on the universal map. He also identifies the needed profinite inputs (trivial centralisers, conjugacy of torsion), which correspond to later profinite free-product results. This anticipates, unpublished, a standard step in the theory of \hat{GT}, but the result itself is known in the literature.
missed.quote: Nous admettrons encore que ces faits s'étendent aux éléments de $\widehat{\pi}_{0,3}$
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and a geometric (fixed-point) proof strategy for the 2-cycle parametrisation in \hat{GT}, including the extended (non-oriented) version with explicit Klein-group indeterminacy.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful and correct, but the content (2-cycle relation ⇔ f = g σ(g)^{-1}, plus the centraliser computation) is known in the GT literature. The main interest is that Grothendieck reached it independently through non-abelian H^1 and fixed points on the universal map.
transcription_corrections: 'qui se réduisent[?] en σ_∞, τ_∞, τ'_∞' probably reads 'qui se notent aussi σ_∞, τ_∞, τ'_∞' or similar.
'(pas seulement β ∈ π)' should read 'et non seulement β ∈ π'.
'dans l'indétermination est dans' should read 'alors l'indétermination est dans'.
(38) likely abbreviates the statement that π̂_{0,3}^{σ_∞} = {1}.
